neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas

developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media

Scattered café au lait macules present on the back

Immunohistochemical staining: Positive: CD33, CD123, CD4, CD163
White blood cell count: 76,400/µL
Annular dusky red indurated plaques on right flank and back with central clearing and trailing scale, scattered café au lait macules
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate (×40 and ×400 magnification)
No family history of NF1

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, along with the histopathological findings of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient's medical history of juvenile xanthogranuloma and the presence of scattered café au lait macules on the back are consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and the presence of café au lait macules are consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient was diagnosed with otitis media, which is a common infection in children.

The patient's presentation of a rash that began with multiple round red patches and did not improve with treatment for a fungal infection, along with the presence of fever, could be consistent with eczema herpeticum.

The patient's presentation of multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, along with the histopathological findings of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, could be consistent with mastocytosis.
The patient's presentation of fever and otitis media, along with the elevated white blood cell count, could be consistent with an infectious etiology.

The patient's presentation of multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, along with the histopathological findings of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, could be consistent with histiocytoid Sweet syndrome.
The histopathology findings of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with positive staining for CD4 and CD163 are consistent with Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome.
